notes: RMG splits its settings over two files, both ini: mupen64plus.cfg (' = ' separator) and GLideN64's own GLideN64.ini (QSettings: '=', backslash keys, the [User] profile section that [General] profile names). Both are seeded, so every patch lands in an anchored file; RMG and GLideN64 rewrite them whole on exit, which the game-level restore journal already handles.
Rendering size is GLideN64's nativeResFactor: 0 renders at the output resolution (GLideN64's default -- why the picture looks upscaled out of the box), N at N times the N64's 320x240.
Widescreen is GLideN64's aspect: 3 (adjust) renders true 16:9 without stretching, 1 is the N64's 4:3. Games draw their HUD for 4:3 either way.

CPU overclocking is the core's CountPerOpDenomPot (cycles per instruction halved when 1). RMG mirrors the key between [Core] and its own Core Overlay section, so a choice writes both and the copy direction never matters.
The video options live in GLideN64.ini and so apply only to GLideN64, the seeded default video plugin.

Video plugin: this AppImage ships exactly two, GLideN64 (GLES) and paraLLEl-RDP (no Rice, Glide64 or Angrylion). paraLLEl-RDP is an LLE RDP: it needs the parallel RSP, so the option writes GFX_Plugin and RSP_Plugin together (GLideN64 pairs back with HLE). It also needs the GPU features the A610/A650 boards lack (8/16-bit SSBO storage -- the reason gopher64 was replaced), so it is for the A7xx boards (SM8550 and newer); elsewhere the game will not start until the choice is put back.

options.label: Rendering size
options.description: Render 3D at a multiple of the N64's 320x240, or at the screen's own resolution. Lower is more authentic, higher is sharper.

options.label: Widescreen (16:9)
options.description: Render 16:9 instead of the N64's 4:3, widening the view without stretching. The HUD of most games stays drawn for 4:3.

options.label: FPS display
options.description: Show the frame rate in the corner of the screen.

options.label: Video plugin
options.description: GLideN64 runs on every board. paraLLEl-RDP is pixel-accurate but needs an SM8550 or newer GPU: on other boards the game will not start with it.

options.label: CPU overclocking
options.description: Emulate an overclocked N64 CPU: smoother in games that slow down on real hardware, but it can break timing-sensitive games.
